is_anopheles.evidence: Insectary-reared Anopheles gambiae s.s. and wild-caught An. gambiae s.l. (identified as An. arabiensis, An. quadriannulatus, and An. merus) were tested (Page 1, Page 9).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study evaluates an ivermectin bio-efficacy assay methodology and does not genotype any of the targeted insecticide resistance markers. The authors state: 'we could not test or screen mosquitoes for this biological trait phenotypically... more work is needed... to further identify resistance markers' (Page 12).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No resistance marker genotype or allele counts/frequencies are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Larvae were collected from breeding sites in Jego village, Kwale county, Coastal Kenya in May 2022 (Page 5).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical methodology study testing ivermectin bio-efficacy on laboratory and wild-caught mosquitoes (Page 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Jego village, Kwale county, Coastal Kenya (Page 5).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito larvae were collected in May 2022 (Page 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original field collection and laboratory bioassay study.

supplement.evidence: No marker genotyping was conducted, so no supplementary genotyping data is required.

assessment.summary: This study develops and evaluates a field-friendly bioassay using a 1:4 blood-to-glucose mixture for assessing ivermectin bio-efficacy in Anopheles gambiae s.l. vectors in Kwale County, Kenya. No insecticide-resistance marker genotyping was carried out.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report any target insecticide resistance markers (e.g., Vgsc, Ace-1, GSTe2, Cyp6p9a/b).
Does not report extractable target marker genotype data.
